pharm: Single-isomer ((R,R)-) long-acting selective beta-2 adrenergic agonist with roughly two-fold greater potency than racemic formoterol; nebulized bronchodilator for COPD maintenance.
quick: 15 mcg nebulized twice daily (morning and evening); max 30 mcg/day
Use only if benefit outweighs fetal risk
Caution; detected in animal milk, human data lacking
FEV1/symptoms, serum K+/glucose, ECG in cardiac disease
summary: Arformoterol is the (R,R)-enantiomer of formoterol, a long-acting beta-2 agonist given by nebulizer for long-term twice-daily maintenance of bronchoconstriction in COPD (chronic bronchitis, emphysema). It is not for acute bronchospasm and is not indicated for asthma; LABA monotherapy increases asthma-related death risk. Standard dose is one 15 mcg unit-dose vial twice daily, not exceeding 30 mcg/day.
indications: Long-term, twice-daily maintenance treatment of bronchoconstriction in patients with COPD, including chronic bronchitis and emphysema

dosage.n: Total daily dose greater than 30 mcg is not recommended

admin: Administer by oral inhalation via a standard jet nebulizer connected to an air compressor; do not swallow the solution
Use only the unit-dose vial; do not mix with other medications in the nebulizer
Take morning and evening doses approximately 12 hours apart
Not for acute relief of bronchospasm; ensure patient has a short-acting rescue bronchodilator
Store refrigerated; protect from light and heat until use
moa: Selective long-acting beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; stimulates intracellular adenyl cyclase, increasing cyclic AMP and causing relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle and inhibition of inflammatory mediator release. The (R,R)-enantiomer has about twice the potency of racemic formoterol.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to arformoterol, racemic formoterol, or any product component
Use as monotherapy (without an inhaled corticosteroid) in patients with asthma
Not indicated for treatment of asthma

preg: Animal studies showed teratogenic effects at high multiples of the recommended dose; use during pregnancy only if expected benefit outweighs potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Arformoterol and metabolites detected in milk of lactating rats; human data insufficient. Weigh developmental/health benefits of breastfeeding against clinical need and potential effects on the infant.
renal: No dose adjustment required; systemic exposure similar to healthy controls.
hepatic: Use cautiously; clearance is prolonged and systemic exposure increased. Monitor closely. No specific dose adjustment provided.

major: Beta-blockers (block effect and may provoke severe bronchospasm)
MAO inhibitors, tricyclic antidepressants, and other QT-prolonging drugs (administer with extreme caution; potentiate cardiovascular effects)
moderate: Non-potassium-sparing diuretics (worsen ECG changes and hypokalemia)
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum potassium and glucose; ECG in patients with cardiac disease.

monitoring: FEV1 and symptom response; increasing rescue inhaler use signals deterioration
Serum potassium (especially with diuretics or xanthines)
Heart rate and ECG in patients with cardiovascular disease
counsel: This is a maintenance medication, NOT for acute symptom relief; always keep a short-acting rescue inhaler
Do not use more than one vial twice a day
Do not mix with other medications in the nebulizer
Do not use with other long-acting beta-agonist medications
Report worsening shortness of breath, increased rescue inhaler use, palpitations, or tremor
Inform your clinician if pregnant or breastfeeding
pk: Refrigerate 2-8 C (36-46 F) in foil pouch; room temperature up to 6 weeks
pearls: Single (R,R)-enantiomer of formoterol with about twice the potency of the racemic mixture
LABA monotherapy is contraindicated in asthma due to increased asthma-related death risk; arformoterol is not approved for asthma
Nebulized formulation is useful for COPD patients who cannot use handheld inhalers
Tolerance to bronchoprotective effect may develop with chronic use
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is near the time of the next dose; do not double up. Resume the regular twice-daily schedule.
overdose: Signs of excessive beta-adrenergic stimulation: tachycardia (up to ~200 bpm), arrhythmias, tremor, headache, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia. Discontinue the drug and provide supportive care; a cardioselective beta-blocker may be considered with caution (risk of bronchospasm). Cardiac monitoring recommended.
